Package org.apache.juneau.rest.server.mcp.v20260728

Class McpResourceServerSupport

java.lang.Object
org.apache.juneau.rest.server.mcp.v20260728.McpResourceServerSupport
public final class McpResourceServerSupport extends Object
Request-time glue for the F2 OAuth 2.1 resource-server baseline — bearer validation, RFC 8707 audience enforcement, 401/403 challenge emission, and RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata construction — driven by an McpResourceServerConfig.

Bearer extraction and token validation are delegated to the reusable OAuthFilter (RFC 6750) from juneau-rest-server-auth-oauth; this class layers on the MCP-specific resource_metadata challenge parameter, RFC 8707 audience matching (McpAudienceValidator), and baseline required-scope enforcement.

Since:
10.0.0

  • Method Details

    • gateMcpEndpoint

      public static void gateMcpEndpoint(McpResourceServerConfig cfg, RestContext ctx, jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest req, jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletResponse res)
      Router-identity bearer gate for the McpEndpoint mixin's MCP JSON-RPC endpoint (READY-312f F2, B1/H3).

      A no-op unless RS auth is enabled and this request resolves to the MCP JSON-RPC dispatch operation. See resolvesToMcpDispatch(RestContext, HttpServletRequest) for how the target operation is identified without any hand-rolled path reconstruction — the key change that makes this gate immune to @Mixin(path/paths) re-mounts and to trailing-slash / percent-encoding / method-override drift.

      Fails fast with the same origin-root 500 diagnostic as the well-known route (see assertWellKnownMountReachable(RestRequest)) — rather than authenticating — whenever the resolved MCP dispatch operation is itself mounted under a @Mixin(path/paths) re-mount prefix (H1 unification): a 401 on such a mount would advertise a resource_metadata URL that the re-mount has already made unreachable, so the two routes must agree rather than leaving a broken half-state.

      Parameters:
      cfg - The RS config. Must not be null.
      ctx - The host RestContext handling this request (injected into the @RestStartCall hook). Must not be null.
      req - The raw HTTP request. Must not be null.
      res - The raw HTTP response (used to emit the challenge header on rejection). Must not be null.

    • gateMcpServlet

      public static void gateMcpServlet(McpResourceServerConfig cfg, jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest req, jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletResponse res)
      Router-aligned bearer gate for the McpRestServlet's POST / endpoint (READY-312f F2, H3).

      A no-op unless RS auth is enabled and this request resolves to a POST (the dedicated MCP servlet's only writable surface). Gating every effective POST is correct for a dedicated MCP servlet: there is no non-MCP writable surface to distinguish, so no per-operation identity check is needed.

      Parameters:
      cfg - The RS config. Must not be null.
      req - The raw HTTP request. Must not be null.
      res - The raw HTTP response (used to emit the challenge header on rejection). Must not be null.

    • authenticate

      public static Principal authenticate(McpResourceServerConfig cfg, jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest req, jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletResponse res)
      Authenticates the request against the RS config, establishing the authenticated principal.

      On success the principal is stashed under RestServerConstants.PRINCIPAL_ATTR and returned. On failure the WWW-Authenticate: Bearer ... challenge (carrying the resource_metadata pointer) is written directly to res — because an exception thrown from a @RestStartCall hook does not route through the response processors that would otherwise copy an AuthenticationException's headers — and then a 401 Unauthorized (AuthenticationException) or 403 Forbidden (insufficient scope) is thrown.

      Parameters:
      cfg - The RS config. Must be enabled and valid.
      req - The HTTP request. Must not be null.
      res - The HTTP response, used to write the challenge header on failure. Must not be null.
      Returns:
      The authenticated principal. Never null.

    • principal

      public static Principal principal(jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest req)
      Returns the authenticated Principal authenticate(org.apache.juneau.rest.server.mcp.v20260728.McpResourceServerConfig, jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest, jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletResponse) stashed for this request (READY-312f F4).

      Reads the same framework-standard RestServerConstants.PRINCIPAL_ATTR attribute authenticate(org.apache.juneau.rest.server.mcp.v20260728.McpResourceServerConfig, jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest, jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletResponse) writes on success, so this is the single source of truth for "who is calling this MCP request". It is the seam the 2026-07-28 dispatcher threads into RequestStateCodec.seal(org.apache.juneau.rest.server.mcp.v20260728.McpRequestState, java.lang.String, java.security.Principal)/RequestStateCodec.unseal(java.lang.String, java.lang.String, java.security.Principal) for principal-bound requestState AAD. Mirrors grantedScopes(HttpServletRequest): a null request, an absent attribute, or a non-Principal value all return null — the anonymous / RS-auth-disabled path, which every caller must handle without an NPE. Unlike grantedScopes(HttpServletRequest), which falls back to an empty Set in that same situation, this returns null rather than an empty value in that case; the divergence is intentional — a scalar identity has no natural "empty" representative the way a collection does.

      Parameters:
      req - The HTTP request. May be null.
      Returns:
      The authenticated principal, or null when none was stashed (RS auth disabled / gate not run / anonymous caller).

    • enforceOperationScopes

      public static void enforceOperationScopes(McpResourceServerConfig cfg, Collection<String> grantedScopes, McpOperationContext ctx)
      Enforces SEP-2350 per-operation step-up scopes at the POST-parse dispatch point.

      A no-op unless RS auth is enabled and the resolved operation has a non-empty required-scope set. When the caller's grantedScopes do not satisfy the operation's required scopes, throws a 403 Forbidden carrying a WWW-Authenticate: Bearer ..., error="insufficient_scope", scope="..." step-up challenge that names exactly the scopes required for this operation.

      This is the enforcement point the F2 security review mandated: unlike the @RestStartCall bearer gate (which fires before the JSON-RPC body is parsed), this runs once the MCP method — and thus the operation — is known, so the challenge can be scoped to the specific operation. It layers on top of, and never weakens, the baseline gate (op-identity, origin-root fail-fast, audience, and baseline required-scope enforcement all still run first in authenticate(org.apache.juneau.rest.server.mcp.v20260728.McpResourceServerConfig, jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest, jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletResponse)).

      Parameters:
      cfg - The RS config. Must not be null.
      grantedScopes - The caller's granted scopes. May be null (treated as empty).
      ctx - The resolved operation. Must not be null.
      Throws:
      Forbidden - 403 insufficient_scope when the granted scopes do not satisfy the operation's required scopes.

    • satisfies

      public static boolean satisfies(Collection<String> grantedScopes, Collection<String> requiredScopes)
      Returns whether the granted scopes satisfy every required scope, honoring OAuth scope hierarchies where a broader granted scope implies its narrower children.

      A required scope r is satisfied when some granted scope g either equals r exactly, or is a hierarchical ancestor of it — i.e. r begins with g followed by a : or . delimiter (so granted repo implies required repo:read / repo.write, but granted repo:read does not imply required repo).

      Parameters:
      grantedScopes - The caller's granted scopes. Never null.
      requiredScopes - The scopes required to invoke the operation. Never null.
      Returns:
      true if every required scope is satisfied.

    • missingTokenChallenge

      public static String missingTokenChallenge(McpResourceServerConfig cfg)
      Builds the WWW-Authenticate challenge for a request that presented no bearer credentials (RFC 6750 §3: no error code).

      Carries a scope hint listing the endpoint-wide baseline required scopes (SEP-2350) when any are configured, so a client can request them on its first authorization; the hint is omitted (no scope="") when no baseline scope is required.

      Parameters:
      cfg - The RS config.
      Returns:
      The challenge value.
